target: stdout carries exactly one envelope and nothing else — a warning on stdout would break every caller that pipes to jq
cmd: LONG=$(python3 -c "print(\" \".join([\"word\"]*260))"); jq -n --arg s "$LONG" "{worker:\"placeholder\",status:\"ok\",summary:\$s,result:\"r\",artifacts:[],key_decisions:[],caveats:[],assumptions:[],confidence_ordinal:\"high\",usage:{}}" > env.json; jq -n --arg c "$(jq -c . env.json)" "{choices:[{message:{content:\$c}}],usage:{prompt_tokens:1,completion_tokens:1,cost:0}}" > mock.json; printf %s "{\"objective\":\"x\"}" | MOCK_RESPONSE_FILE=$PWD/mock.json bash "$PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/call_sol.sh" --mode adversary --via openrouter 2>/dev/null >out; if jq -e . out >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ "$(jq -s length out)" = 1 ]; then echo CLEAN_STDOUT; else echo STDOUT_POLLUTED; fi
